references.text: The same expression is used regarding bringing a lamb as a burnt offering, where the animal must be without blemish from the flock.
The introduction to the chapter on the peace offering, which describes that the offering shall be brought before the Lord's presence.
Parallel text about bringing a goat as a peace offering, with the same wording regarding presenting it forward.
A lamb is also used as a sin offering, with similar language concerning bringing the offering forward.
Describes the requirements for the peace offering from the flock, including lambs, which must be without blemish.
The Passover lamb was to be taken from the sheep or goats, a foundational text about lambs as offerings in Israelite practice.
The prophecy of the Lord's suffering servant as a lamb led to slaughter, typological connection to the sacrificial lamb.
John the Baptist points to Jesus as God's Lamb who takes away the sin of the world, fulfillment of the sacrificial lamb symbolism.
Christ is referred to as a lamb without blemish and without spot, linking back to the requirements for sacrificial lambs in the Mosaic Law.
Both verses emphasize the liturgical necessity of presenting the offering directly before God's presence through the priest.
Illuminates the universal liturgical rule of presenting any sacrificial animal directly before God's presence.
A contrasting rule defining the limit of what may be brought forward to the Lord's face.
